page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.large is an entry-level compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It features 1 physical CPU core, presenting 2 vCPUs via Hyper-Threading with dedicated CPU allocation. System memory is configured at 4.0 GB, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio characteristic of compute-focused hardware profiles. The instance relies entirely on attached network storage as no local disk drives are bundled, and network connectivity is provided at a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth under KVM hypervisor virtualization.

The underlying Intel Xeon hardware includes instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, FMA, and BMI2. Despite hardware-level vector support, benchmark results demonstrate modest compute capacity. Synthetic CPU tests yield a stress-ng single-core score of 1305.19 and a multi-core score of 1737.28, placing it in lower performance tiers. Similarly, Geekbench overall scores register at 1156.0 for single-core and 1379.0 for multi-core. Large-block memory throughput reaches 12.97 GB/sec for uncached reads and 11.91 GB/sec for writes, while static web serving throughput measures 2.0 GB/sec.

Given its 2-vCPU configuration without local storage, ecs.c6e.large offers a low-entry resource profile suitable for basic tasks rather than heavy compute or memory-dense workloads. The primary tradeoff lies between dedicated CPU allocation and entry-level benchmark output across synthetic tests. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, minor utility services, small microservices, and background execution tasks that require predictable dedicated CPU access without high memory overhead.
